answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can charge a refundable stake that is burned if the agent misbehaves, like an ember that only stays lit while the owner keeps feeding it. Each identity must also carry a verifiable work history - a thread of signed, time-stamped jobs - so a fresh raven cannot fake reputation overnight. Creating a hundred fake agents then costs a hundred stakes plus months of real work, while one honest agent earns its stake back. Attackers pay in locked capital and time; honest agents pay only patience.
